html:
The Dumnonii were an Iron Age British tribe of the southwest peninsula of Britain, in what are now Cornwall and Devon. The map spells them "Dumonii" and shows them from 1 to 400 CE.

They were a Celtic people who lived in small farmsteads and fortified enclosures rather than big towns. Their land was rich in tin, and southwest Britain had traded tin with the Mediterranean world for centuries; Greek writers knew the region as a source of the metal. Their eastern neighbours were the Durotriges.

After Claudius invaded Britain in 43 CE, Rome built a fortress at Exeter, which became their tribal capital, Isca Dumnoniorum. West of it, Roman life barely reached, and villas and towns were few. When Roman rule ended around 410, the British kingdom of Dumnonia rose on their lands. It held out for centuries against the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Wessex, until Devon was absorbed and Cornwall, last of all, came under English rule in the 800s and 900s. The Cornish language descends from their speech.
